specification.problem: Evaluate a single ternary majority gate MAJ3(x1,x2,x3) on an explicit classical input x by building a span-program-derived weighted bipartite graph, compiling its adjacency matrix into a unitary, and applying a phase-estimation-style spectral test for the eigenvalue-zero eigenvector with root support.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Single depth-1 MAJ3 gate with explicit classical input x compiled into gates. No recursive formula composition, no balanced-formula optimality, no query-complexity claim. The exact MAJ3 span program and graph weights are background or assumption, not given in the abstract. A concrete weighted graph and phase-estimation schedule are not fully fixed here.

symbols.meaning: Span program with target t and input vectors v_i
Target vector of the span program
Weighted bipartite graph built from P and x
Symmetric weighted adjacency matrix of G(x)
Unitary exp(iA s) with s a gap-scale time (assumption)
Phase-estimation precision, below the smallest nonzero |eigenvalue| scale

equations.label: MAJ3 definition
equations.justification: Definition of 3-majority, named in the abstract only by name.

equations.label: Span program acceptance
equations.description: Span program evaluates to 1 when the target lies in the span of the available input vectors
equations.justification: Standard span-program definition; abstract mentions span programs only as a linear-algebraic model of computation.
assumptions: A valid MAJ3 span program P is chosen, e.g. any two available inputs span t and a single one does not

equations.label: Graph eigenvector correspondence
equations.description: Evaluation corresponds to a zero-eigenvalue eigenvector of the graph, with root overlap as the decision criterion
equations.abstract_quote: A span program's evaluation corresponds to an eigenvalue-zero eigenvector of the associated graph.
equations.justification: The abstract states the correspondence qualitatively. The root-overlap criterion is an assumed refinement, and the precise graph construction is not given.
assumptions: Root-support formulation; exact graph weights are a modeling choice

equations.label: Unitary from graph
equations.description: Bipartite adjacency block form compiled into a unitary; eigenvalue 0 gives phase 0
equations.justification: Hamiltonian simulation of the adjacency matrix is a standard route to spectral estimation; the choice of s and the simulation method are assumed.
assumptions: Explicit classical matrix compiled to gates, e.g. exact matrix exponential synthesis for a tiny instance
s*||A||<pi so phases do not alias

equations.label: Zero-phase probability
equations.description: Probability that phase estimation on |r> reads the zero-eigenvalue bin
equations.justification: Standard phase estimation applied to |r> decomposed in the eigenbasis of A, ignoring leakage from finite precision. The abstract states only that spectral estimation is used.
assumptions: Gap between 0 and the smallest nonzero |eigenvalue| exceeds the precision

registers.name: vertex
registers.size: ceil(log2 |V|) qubits, basis states indexed by graph vertices
registers.role: Holds the graph vertex state; initial state is the root vertex

registers.name: phase
registers.size: m qubits with 2^m large relative to 1/epsilon
registers.role: Phase estimation register, left unmeasured by the measurement-free circuit

specification.initial_state: vertex register in |r> (root vertex basis state), phase register in |0^m>

steps.description: Fix the MAJ3 span program P (background or assumption) and build the bipartite graph G(x) by keeping only edges for inputs with x_i=1.
Form the adjacency matrix A and compile U=exp(iAs) classically into gates, with controlled powers U^(2^k).
Apply Hadamards to the phase register, controlled powers of U, and the inverse QFT on the phase register.

specification.measurement: Read the phase register externally; outcome 0 (zero-eigenvalue bin) indicates a zero eigenvector with root overlap, i.e. formula value per the correspondence. The returned circuit itself is measurement-free.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Threshold p_0 compared with a constant, with repetition if needed; the threshold is an assumption.
assumptions: The smallest useful construction is a single MAJ3 gate with explicit x
The span program and graph weights are a chosen standard construction, not from the abstract
Adjacency compiled explicitly into gates, with no black-box or query-count claim
Root-overlap decision rule and the time s are assumptions
missing_information: Exact graph construction and edge weights from the paper
Handling of the case where the root has small overlap on the zero eigenspace
Optimality claims for the balanced ternary majority formula, not reproduced
